item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 28 October 2026
item.description:
Tipa digs Willy and Charlie: Solitaire as a head-to-head deckbuilding solitaire mashup with faction cards, carryover strategy, and some delightfully busted shop upgrades.

Bhagpuss wraps up Steam Next Fest demos, praising Hela: of Mice & Magic for its polished, no-save confidence and surprisingly winning mouse adventure.

Ramen Junkie finds Transformers One’s Studio Series Elita-1 impressively complex but frustratingly fiddly, with clean looks undermined by parts that won’t stay put.

Wilhelm heads deeper into Over the Hill, where Gimli Ridge’s swamps, janky physics, and a nerve-wracking boardwalk make mud-driving sound weirdly compelling.

Kelly posts a piece titled Michael (Mikhail) Bennett is AI generated, but the excerpt provided doesn’t include enough of the argument to say more.

Jeff Atwood spotlights dreamagainusa.org, using endless scrolling to make America’s wealth inequality feel brutally experiential instead of abstract.

Joar hands things to Yoshi, whose dog’s-eye review of the Ohio-to-Arizona move is anxious, funny, and extremely hard on hotels.

Juhis shares an early Obsidian prototype that publishes individual notes as temporary, private URLs via Hermes and Agora—basically lightweight note-sharing without SaaS baggage.

Jeff documents a niche but handy Noctua fan swap for a Calnex Rb/GPS frequency reference, mainly to make his atomic-clock gear desk-friendly.

Mike gets CamelForth booting on real SG-1000 hardware, with the Soggy-1000 and an original SK-1100 keyboard proving emulator theory in practice.

Dave Winer argues the web’s old model is ending, and pitches BigUndo, RSS, and Markdown as the small-parts path forward.

Tofutush offers a brisk, approachable primer on reading Arabic script via Uyghurche examples, covering letter forms, connections, and the truly evil non-connectors.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 27 October 2026
item.description:
Anarchae’s Divinity: Original Sin 2 session brings skinks, soul jars, Trompdoy illusions, and the special pain of accidentally donating 400 gold in loot.

UltrViolet finds WoW Forever is basically WoW Classic with a modern UI—less self-punishing, still grindy, and not exactly inspiring spontaneous grouping.

Shintar hits level 100 in SWTOR Galactic Season 11, feels the companion-heavy objectives drag, and is very ready for Masters of the Force news.

Azuriel finishes Valheim 1.0 after 118 hours and argues the no-metal-through-portals rule adds more logistics slog than meaningful challenge.

Welsh Troll digs into Torchlight 2’s surprising new beta branch, with Steam matchmaking, controller support, fixes, and some AI-assisted codebase archaeology.

Marc traces how Taito’s basic Ninja Warriors became the much richer Ninja Saviors, a robo-ninja beat ’em up with real crowd-control depth.

Wilhelm wraps up the WoW Forever beta, side-eyes Reddit outrage, and waits to see how layering and launch land with the real crowd.

Joel’s weeknotes bounce from Outer Wilds: Echoes of the Eye and Dune Messiah to card tricks, trip prep, and an unexpected patio dog.

Syp celebrates the iPod’s 25th with modded Classics, porch listening, and a reminder that Apple killed a gadget some people still genuinely love.

Warner puzzles over the iPhone Duo’s sidebar-heavy UI and wonders why Apple’s Liquid Glass ambitions don’t seem to show up here.

Bruce Schneier flags research showing AI models can hide arbitrary capabilities behind secret triggers, which is a pretty grim limit on audit-by-elicitation.

Cristian shares a video roundup of 20 desk setup upgrades that supposedly actually matter, aimed squarely at practical workspace tinkerers.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 26 October 2026
item.description:
Tipa says EverQuest Legends’ Halloween drop revived the game with Ayr’Haeth, Lake Nerius, and Nektropos Castle giving lapsed players a reason back.

Roger mourns BioWare’s closure as another brutal industry contraction, with Dragon Age and Mass Effect giving way to cuts and safer bets.

Frostilyte detours through Union Cave to prep a scrappy Pokémon Silver team for the Radio Tower, with a side gripe about roaming legendaries.

Bhagpuss makes the case for Once Human’s Isles of Abyss, calling it underrated despite its messy identity as survival crafter, FPS, MMO, and gacha.

Ellie finds Tiny Bookshop a cozy bookselling sim whose real charm is Bookstonbury itself, all wistful seaside vibes and literary atmosphere.

Wilhelm tracks Fantasy Critic’s home stretch as Final Fantasy Resonance, Modern Warfare 4, Planet Zoo 2, and Toem 2 jostle a tightening scoreboard.

The Chronicler teaches Lone U-Boat by playing a mission, spotlighting detection, depth, escorts, and a couple easy-to-make rules slips.

The Friendly Necromancer walks through EverQuest Legends’ Nektropos Castle access quest, from Lake Nerius errands to harpsichord-fixing key shenanigans.

JJM finally ships Outpost for ZX Spectrum 48k, built around colored sprites, interrupt-driven beeper audio, and floating-bus tricks to cut flicker.

Emily pushes back on the ‘when are you replacing it?’ small talk, arguing a well-running used car beats treating vehicles like status symbols.

Tan weighs Britain’s new disaster-prep push against the realities of inequality, climate shocks, cyberattacks, and the slow grind of recurring crisis.

Nicole digs into Mahjong Bakuhatsu Junjouden’s odd Nichibutsu hardware, from dual Z80s to a custom 1413M3 chip and blitter-driven quirks.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 25 October 2026
item.description:
Anarchae’s Divinity: Original Sin 2 trek through Hollow Marshes brings undead, necrofire pigs, trap bulbs, and more hotbar-management pain.

CrazyKinux chats with Bluedagger about EVE Online wormholes, evictions, hauling headaches, and a CSM pitch to make Sleepers and Drifters nastier.

Sey rounds up indie picks including Virtue and a Sledgehammer, Scramble Knights Online, tinymancer, and a Kickstarter push for Mirage: Miracle Quest.

Krista highlights Steam Next Fest standouts, spotlighting cozy demos and hidden gems like Spirit Crossing, Book Nook, Littlelands, and ReShine.

Margot’s week is part Retroid Pocket Duo shipping anxiety, part spooky-game check-in, with some Nintendo DS and 3DS nostalgia on the side.

Shintar digs into why World of Warcraft players are furious at patch 12.1.5, arguing Liadrin’s big sacrifice stumbles in the execution.

Wilhelm runs through gaming’s grim week: BioWare shuttered, Xbox layoffs pile up, and cloud-gaming pricing looks like another bad plan.

Tobold eyes Spiel 2026’s hottest board games and wonders whether flashy table presence beats the very real pain of long, hard-to-table sessions.

Andrew Plotkin loves Nivalis Nights for its grimy neon city vibes, even as the noodle-bar sim turns out way more intricate than expected.

Kelly makes the blunt case that back-to-office mandates hurt productivity, flexibility, and older workers who built their lives around remote work.

Ramen Junkie’s wrap-up is a fun grab bag of toy pickups, mini arcades, Bubble Man, Zangief, Lara Croft, and Transformers vinyl.

Dave Winer jumps from the Knicks to rssCloud/WebSub-over-WebSockets and the Web of Markdown, all while plotting a new home beyond Google.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 24 October 2026
item.description:
Azuriel argues BioWare’s closure wasn’t just EA cruelty, pointing to repeated mismanagement, crunch, and Frostbite as the longer collapse.

Joel finally finishes Final Fantasy IV on PSP and comes away charmed by Cecil’s story, classic party design, and the series’ turning point.

Luna wraps week three of Spooktober with Bloomtown, This Bed We Made, Slay the Princess, and a late add: Gloomy Eyes.

Joar gets why WoW Forever exists, but would rather spend limited MMO time on current WoW, Aion 2, and Midnight than revisit vanilla.

Cind Swanson traces Epic’s trend-chasing history into 7th Legion, tying the RTS detour to the company’s long-running bad vibes.

Wilhelm rounds up EVE Online’s Fractured Skies, CSM21 voting, and assorted New Eden odds and ends with cautious, slightly weary commentary.

Jimmy digs into Ion Storm through Stevie Case’s rise from Quake competitor to a key figure in that late-90s gaming orbit.

Tofutush answers a 100-question meme with OC brainworms, Henry Stickmin nostalgia, karaoke My Little Pony, and delightfully chaotic energy.

Aywren mourns BioWare, winces at a major PHP security mess disrupting sites like FFXIV, and ends on a cautiously hopeful personal note.

Juhis shares a debugging faceplant from Django tests and Stripe settings, a solid reminder that assumptions will absolutely waste your day.

Warner says iPhone Duo reviews mostly confirmed the obvious, while Apple’s late app-readiness PR only made the rollout look sloppier.

Tim Bray wrestles with using GenAI on Quamina, balancing ethical unease against the very real temptation to offload tricky data-format work.
